title: When Generated Information Returns: Error Persistence in LLM-Mediated Information Ecosystems
abstract: arXiv:2610.33617v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly produce online articles from material that later becomes input to other models. This circulation connects individual responses to the information available for subsequent generation. We study a consequential distinction: an article can avoid endorsing a false claim while preserving the concrete details that enable its reproduction. Our framework connects claim content, expressed stance, and downstream reuse to explain selective error persistence under a continuing supply of accurate and inaccurate information. We implement a controlled community writing process that varies whether published articles return as inputs, matching external supply, input capacity, and generation volume. Across twelve factual targets and four production models, recirculation increases the presence of complete false claims by 7.29 percentage points at the final round while reducing explicit endorsement by 8.33 points. translated_title: 当生成信息回归时：LLM介导的信息生态系统中的错误持续性
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）日益基于某些材料生成在线文章，而这些材料随后会成为其他模型的输入。这种循环将单个模型的响应与后续生成可用的信息联系起来。我们研究了一个具有重要影响的区别：一篇文章可以在避免明确认可虚假声明的同时，保留使其能够被复现的具体细节。我们的框架将声明内容、表达立场和下游复用联系起来，以解释在准确与不准确信息持续供应的情况下错误为何会被选择性地持续保留。我们实现了一个受控的社区写作过程，通过改变已发布文章是否作为输入回流，并匹配外部供应、输入容量和生成数量进行实验。在十二个事实目标和四个生产级模型上，再循环使最后一轮完整虚假声明的出现率增加了7.29个百分点，同时使明确认可减少了8.33个百分点。
tldr: 该研究揭示了LLM信息生态中的错误持续性机制：当模型生成的内容回流作为其他模型的输入时，文章会以“不明确认可但保留可复现细节”的方式选择性传播错误，再循环使完整虚假声明增加7.29个百分点。
en_tdlr: When LLM-generated articles recirculate as inputs to other models, errors persist selectively—content avoids explicitly endorsing false claims while preserving the concrete details needed for their reproduction, increasing complete false claims by 7.29 percentage points in the final round.
